description: Deterministic tie-break conformance vectors for AprioriMining. When rules share identical lift, confidence, and evidenceCount, the four-key total order resolves ties lexicographically by (antecedent packed keys ASC, consequent packed key ASC). Swift and Rust must produce bit-identical output.
notes: Item.packed = (field << 8) | value. For field=0: A=(0,1) packed=1, B=(0,2) packed=2, C=(0,3) packed=3.

cases.name: all_equal_metrics_resolve_lexicographically
cases.description: Three co-occurring items (A,B,C always together), maxK=2. All six pairwise rules have lift=1.0, confidence=1.0, evidenceCount=3. Tie-break must order by (antecedent.packed, consequent.packed) ascending.
invariants: output identical between Swift and Rust

cases.name: distinct_metrics_unaffected_by_tiebreak
cases.description: am-002 fixture. The two rules differ in confidence (1.0 vs 0.75), so the third sort key (evidenceCount) and fourth (lexicographic) never fire. Output unchanged by the tie-break addition — regression guard.
invariants: metrics unchanged from pre-tie-break am-002 output
